title: Isolate rate limiter and billing for ephemeral proxy token shadowing across subaccounts
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Summary: Short-lived (ephemeral) proxy tokens that shadow longer-lived API keys are intermittently causing resource attribution inversion: rate-limiter counters and billing meters are credited to the wrong tenant when a token swap/rebind happens concurrently with request bursts. This manifests as quota exhaustion on one project while a different project accrues the metered usage. The bug appears when the proxy token TTL and the claim propagation window overlap and the attribution lookup falls back to a cached alias that has been re-bound to a different subaccount. Business impact: incorrect billing, throttling of active customers, support escalations, and potential over/under-charging. Goal: implement deterministic attribution for ephemeral proxy handoffs, prevent counter bleed, and provide a backward reconciliation/meter correction path for recently-affected windows.
observed_behavior: When an ephemeral proxy token is created to forward requests for an ephemeral job (k8s-sidecar, CI runner), and a concurrent rebind/alias operation changes which subaccount the underlying master key points to, we observe: (1) incoming token-bearing requests increment rate-limiter counters scoped to the prior tenant identity for up to 30s, (2) billing events are stamped with a stale tenant id and emitted to billing pipeline, (3) downstream quota service denies traffic for the true owner while another tenant's quota gets consumed. Logs show repeated 'tenant_lookup: cache_hit' entries with different owner ids around the swap window.
expected_behavior: Attribution should be atomic and canonical per-request. During a token swap the system should: (a) resolve tenant identity deterministically (strong read-through to authoritative store), (b) ensure rate-limiter and metering counters are partitioned by the resolved identity and use idempotent increment semantics to avoid double-counting, and (c) surface audit events tying both old/new bindings to the request for forensics without allowing bleed.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create master API key A bound to subaccount alpha
2) Issue ephemeral proxy token T that delegates to A with short TTL (10s)
3) In parallel, rebind master key A to subaccount beta (simulate operator migration)
4) Generate a burst of inbound requests carrying token T during the rebind window
5) Observe rate-limiter counters and billing events attributed to alpha while requests are accepted for beta after rebind completes
scope_and_affected_surface: Hosts using ephemeral delegation (CI runners, sidecars, short-lived worker pools), the rate-limiter service, the metering/billing ingestion pipeline, and the tenant-cache layer. Initial telemetry shows ~120 customers affected intermittently in the last 7 days, with 18 support tickets and 6 potential invoice discrepancies flagged as high-risk.
proposed_solution: A. Attribution circuit change: make tenant-resolution authoritative by performing a synchronous lookup against the tenant-claims store on first use and write a signed ephemeral attribution token for downstream services to validate (instead of relying on in-memory alias cache)
B. Rate-limiter isolation: tag counters with attribution-token-id and use per-token buckets until the attribution is reconciled; do not transfer counters between tenant ids mid-flight
C. Metering emission fix: attach both binding provenance and a monotonic token generation id to billing events; billing pipeline will use token-gen-id to dedupe/assign to canonical tenant

D. Backfill tooling: implement a reconciler job that scans recent billing windows (T-72h) for events where token-gen-id conflicts with current binding and emits corrective adjustments with audit trail
E. Short-term mitigation: increase TTL of read-through attribution cache to 2s and add a reconciliation hook that refuses rebinds while active ephemeral tokens exist (operator-level knob)
F. Add canary and feature flag to toggle new authoritative resolution at edge for measured rollout
rollout_plan: 1) Land rate-limiter tagging + attribution-token generation in staging and run internal stress harness (48h)
2) Enable canary (5% of traffic) in sandbox customers; monitor attribution mismatch rate and quota-deny anomalies
3) After 48h and thresholds met, expand to 30% then 100% across hosted API
4) Run reconciler backfill with dry-run reports for 72h, review with finance before applying corrective billing adjustments
5) Communicate with affected customers (support + ops playbook) and provide exportable audit logs per tenant
tests_and_validation: Integration tests that simulate concurrent rebind + burst traffic and assert no cross-tenant increments
Load tests to measure extra latency introduced by authoritative lookup (target <5ms p50 increase)
E2E billing pipeline dry-runs to ensure dedupe based on token-gen-id
risks_and_mitigation: Extra sync lookups could increase p50 latency: mitigate by caching signed attribution tokens and a canary ramp
Backfill might alter invoices: run dry-run and coordinate with finance/legal and support before applying changes
Operator experience when refusing rebinds: add admin override and telemetry to show active ephemeral token counts
